title: The represented kernel relation of a surjective etale scheme map to an fppf sheaf
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $F$ a sheaf of sets on the big fppf site of $S$ [def-pc-fppf-site]. For an $S$-scheme $W$, write $h_W(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,W)$. Let $U$ be an $S$-scheme and let $p:h_U\to F$ be representable, surjective and etale, in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $R$ be any $S$-scheme with maps $s,t:R\to U$ such that $(h_R,h_s,h_t)$ represents the sheaf fibre product $h_U\times_Fh_U$. Then for every $S$-scheme $T$, the map $r\mapsto(s\circ r,t\circ r)$ is a bijection
$$R(T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{(a,b)\in U(T)^2:p_T(a)=p_T(b)\}.$$
These bijections commute with restriction in $T$. In particular $(s,t):R\to U\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is a monomorphism and its image on $T$-points is an equivalence relation on $U(T)$. Both $s$ and $t$ are surjective etale morphisms of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]. The diagonal $U\to R$ has both composites with $s,t$ equal to $1_U$, and the factor interchange induces an involution $R\to R$ interchanging $s$ and $t$. No representability of the diagonal of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: The Lean hypothesis already gives a pullback of presheaves. Apply IsPullback.map to evaluation at each S-scheme T; evaluation preserves limits in the functor category. Mathlib PullbackCone.IsLimit.equivPullbackObj identifies the evaluated pullback with the subtype of pairs of maps into U whose p-images agree. Its two projection equations give beta_T(r)=(r >> s,r >> t). Associativity proves compatibility with precomposition. No additional sheaf-limit theorem is required for this hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), applied to the finite pullback diagram; spaces.tex Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), first paragraph of proof

proof.text: Use the sectionwise equivalence to prove that a pair (a,b) is in the image of (s,t) exactly when p_T(a)=p_T(b). Equality is an equivalence relation, so this proves reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity. For the map j:R->U times_S U from [def-pc-fibre-product], regard the target as an object over S. Equality after j implies equality after each projection, and injectivity of beta_T implies equality of maps to R. Thus j is mono in Over S; Over.mono_left_of_mono gives the claimed monomorphism of underlying schemes.

source.place: Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), first paragraph of proof: the pointwise equality relation

proof.text: For a scheme morphism property P respecting isomorphisms, any given representing pullback inherits P from the scheme-test definition [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Choose a scheme test W->T; uniqueness of the two pullbacks gives an isomorphism of their representing presheaves. The fully faithful Yoneda embedding [lem-pc-representable-unique] lifts it to e:V~=W with e.hom >> w=v. Then P(v) follows from P(w) by precomposition with an isomorphism. Apply this proved private lemma with P=Surjective and P=Etale to hR and hR.flip. This proves both geometric properties of both projections, using no diagonal condition.

source.place: Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), first paragraph of proof, and definition-relative-representable-property: apply the property to the test map p

proof.text: The image characterization applied at T=U to the identity pair (id_U,id_U) gives d:U->R with d >> s=id_U and d >> t=id_U. The beta formula and associativity also identify its restriction with the diagonal pair at every T.

source.place: Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), equality relation in the first proof paragraph: explicit diagonal

proof.text: The identity of R exhibits (s,t) in the relation, hence p_R(s)=p_R(t). Symmetry of this equality and the image characterization produce i:R->R with i >> s=t and i >> t=s. The beta formula, these two equations and associativity give beta_R(i >> i)=beta_R(id_R). Injectivity of beta_R gives i >> i=id_R. Precomposition and associativity give factor interchange on all test sections.

source.place: Tag 0262 (lemma-space-presentation), equality relation in the first proof paragraph: explicit factor interchange

lean.statement: theorem representable_etale_kernel_relation {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ F.obj) (hrep : IsRepresentable p) (hsur : IsSurjective p) (het : IsEtale p) (R : Over S) (s t : R ⟶ U) (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) p p) : (∃ β : ∀ T : Over S, (T ⟶ R) ≃ {ab : (T ⟶ U) × (T ⟶ U) | p.app (op T) ab.1 = p.app (op T) ab.2}, (∀ (T : Over S) (r : T ⟶ R), (β T r).val = (r ≫ s, r ≫ t)) ∧ ∀ (T T' : Over S) (g : T' ⟶ T) (r : T ⟶ R), (β T' (g ≫ r)).val = (g ≫ (β T r).val.1, g ≫ (β T r).val.2)) ∧ Mono (pullback.lift s.left t.left (s.w.trans t.w.symm)) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ U ↦ ∃ r : T ⟶ R, r ≫ s = a ∧ r ≫ t = b)) ∧ Surjective s.left ∧ Etale s.left ∧ Surjective t.left ∧ Etale t.left ∧ (∃ d : U ⟶ R, d ≫ s = 𝟙 U ∧ d ≫ t = 𝟙 U) ∧ ∃ i : R ⟶ R, i ≫ s = t ∧ i ≫ t = s ∧ i ≫ i = 𝟙 R
